scheme_name: Scheme on Promotion of Use of Liquid Fermented Organic Manure (LFOM) for Increasing Organic Carbon in Soil
description:
The Scheme on Promotion of Use of Liquid Fermented Organic Manure (LFOM) for Increasing Organic Carbon in Soil was launched by the Government of India in the year 2020. 

This scheme is part of the broader initiative to promote sustainable agricultural practices in India. 

The primary objective of the LFOM scheme is to enhance soil fertility and improve the organic carbon content in agricultural soils. 

The scheme aims to increase the organic carbon content in soil by at least 0.5 percent over a period of five years. 

This increase in organic carbon is expected to improve soil health, enhance crop productivity, and promote sustainable farming practices. 

The government has set a target to cover approximately 1 million hectares of agricultural land under this scheme by the end of 2025. 

The benefits of the LFOM scheme include improved soil structure, increased water retention capacity, and enhanced nutrient availability for crops. 

Farmers participating in the scheme can expect an increase in crop yields by up to 20 percent due to improved soil health. 

The scheme also aims to reduce the dependency on chemical fertilizers, thereby promoting environmental sustainability. 

Under this scheme, financial assistance is provided to farmers for the production and application of LFOM. 

Farmers can receive a subsidy of up to 50 percent on the cost of producing LFOM. 

The maximum subsidy amount is capped at INR 50,000 per farmer per year. 

Eligibility for the LFOM scheme is primarily targeted at small and marginal farmers. 

Farmers must own less than 2 hectares of agricultural land to qualify for the scheme. 

Additionally, farmers must be registered under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme to be eligible for benefits. 

The application process for the LFOM scheme involves several steps. 

First, interested farmers must approach the local agricultural department office. 

Farmers need to fill out an application form which is available at the office or can be downloaded from the official website. 

The application form requires details such as the farmer's name, address, land ownership details, and bank account information. 

Farmers must also submit documents such as land ownership proof, identity proof, and PM-KISAN registration details. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be verified by the agricultural department officials. 

After verification, eligible farmers will receive an approval notification. 

The subsidy amount will be disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account. 

The disbursement of subsidies is typically done within 30 days of approval. 

The LFOM scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The National Centre of Organic Farming under the Ministry oversees the operational aspects of the scheme. 

Farmers can contact the local agricultural department for any queries related to the scheme. 

The contact details of the local agricultural department can be found on the official website of the Ministry of Agriculture. 

The scheme also encourages farmers to adopt organic farming practices and reduce chemical inputs. 

Workshops and training sessions are organized to educate farmers about the benefits of LFOM. 

The government also provides technical support for the production of LFOM. 

Farmers are trained on the methods of preparing LFOM using locally available organic materials. 

The LFOM can be produced using materials such as cow dung, kitchen waste, and agricultural residues. 

The fermentation process typically takes about 15 to 20 days. 

Farmers are encouraged to apply LFOM during the land preparation stage before sowing crops. 

The application of LFOM can be done using drip irrigation systems or through manual application. 

The LFOM scheme is expected to contribute significantly to the national goal of increasing organic farming area to 30 million hectares by 2025. 

As of 2023, the government has reported that over 200,000 farmers have benefited from the LFOM scheme. 

The scheme has been instrumental in promoting the use of organic fertilizers in states such as Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh. 

These states have reported an increase in soil organic carbon levels by an average of 0.3 percent since the scheme's implementation. 

The LFOM scheme aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) set by the United Nations, particularly Goal 2 which aims to end hunger and promote sustainable agriculture. 

The scheme is part of the larger National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) launched in 2014. 

The NMSA aims to promote sustainable agricultural practices that enhance productivity while conserving natural resources. 

The LFOM scheme is also linked to the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY) which focuses on irrigation efficiency. 

Farmers using LFOM have reported improved water retention in soils, reducing the need for frequent irrigation. 

The Ministry of Agriculture conducts regular assessments to monitor the progress of the LFOM scheme. 

Feedback from farmers is collected to improve the implementation process and address any challenges faced. 

The government also collaborates with agricultural universities and research institutions for research and development related to LFOM. 

Studies are being conducted to evaluate the long-term impact of LFOM on soil health and crop productivity. 

The LFOM scheme is expected to play a crucial role in India's transition towards sustainable agriculture. 

By promoting organic farming practices, the scheme aims to improve the livelihoods of farmers while ensuring food security for the nation. 

The government continues to encourage more farmers to participate in the LFOM scheme through various outreach programs. 

As of now, the scheme has received positive feedback from the agricultural community. 

Farmers have expressed satisfaction with the financial assistance and the training provided under the scheme. 

The LFOM scheme represents a significant step towards achieving a more sustainable and environmentally friendly agricultural sector in India. 

The government remains committed to supporting farmers in adopting innovative practices that enhance soil health and agricultural productivity. 

In conclusion, the LFOM scheme is a comprehensive initiative aimed at promoting the use of liquid fermented organic manure to improve soil health and increase organic carbon content. 

The scheme provides financial assistance and technical support to farmers, encouraging sustainable agricultural practices across the country.
